stories.title: Genetic interaction between Adgrg6 and Sox9 reveals a feedforward mechanism for postnatal spinal stability
stories.description: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is the most common pediatric spinal disorder and is best understood as a complex polygenic condition. Genome-wide association studies have identified AIS risk loci, including regions near ADGRG6 and SOX9, yet the mechanisms underlying its heritability remain poorly defined. Here we use spatial transcriptomics to characterize gene expression in the spine of a conditional Adgrg6 mutant mouse model, revealing reduced expression of Sox9 and several extracellular matrix genes in the intervertebral disc. We demonstrate a strong genetic interaction between conditional loss of Adgrg6 and a hypomorphic Sox9 allele that increases the penetrance and severity of scoliosis. We further show that SOX9 occupies open chromatin within the Adgrg6 locus in SOX9+ cells isolated from the mouse disc tissue, consistent with direct transcriptional regulation, and provide evidence for SOX9-dependent and SOX9-independent regulation across a variety of spinal tissues. Together, these findings support a self-reinforcing feedforward circuit in which Adgrg6 and Sox9 are co-regulated to maintain extracellular matrix gene expression in the annulus fibrosus and paraspinal tissues. These results provide mechanistic insight into genes implicated by AIS-associated loci and establish combined Adgrg6–Sox9 insufficiency in mice as a tractable model of polygenic scoliosis susceptibility.

stories.title: Viral etiology and predictors of hospitalization in adults younger than 65 years with laboratory-confirmed respiratory viral infections in the pre-COVID era
stories.description: Respiratory viral tract infections (VRTIs) are generally considered more severe in older adults, while their clinical impact in younger adults remains less well characterized. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of adults aged 18–64 years with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), or parainfluenza virus (PIV) infection during the 2016–2018 respiratory seasons. Among 172 patients, 110 had influenza, 31 RSV, 17 hMPV, and 14 PIV infections. Hospitalization occurred in 64.0% of patients overall, with rates of 53.6% for influenza, 77.4% for RSV, and 87.1% for hMPV/PIV infections. Chronic respiratory disease, neutrophilia, and hMPV/PIV infection were independently associated with hospitalization. Chronic respiratory disease and previous respiratory tract infection were independently associated with lower odds of short-term favorable outcome, whereas detectable eosinophils were associated with improved recovery. Ninety-day mortality was low across viral groups. Age was not independently associated with hospitalization or short-term recovery within this restricted age range. These findings highlight substantial morbidity associated with VRTIs in adults younger than 65 years and underscore the need for greater attention to this population, which remains less well characterized than older adults.
